description: Use this when the person wants something tracked over time and no ready-made track or shared template fits. Makes a new kind of sheet with the columns the person agreed to: show them the columns first and wait for a yes or their changes. Rows come from forwarded emails (source email, then add a hack with suggest_hack and save_hack), from an app or Shortcut posting JSON (source webhook), or from the phone's health data (source health: give each health column its health value, and choose health_rows: the TrackerHacker phone app sends a row a day, an hour, a workout or a reading from Apple Health or Health Connect). The person chooses what to track: any value the phone has, how it's combined, and how often. Tell the person every line of tell_the_person. Show an email address they'll copy in a code block (it gets a copy button), and each long link as a named Markdown link, like [Your sheet](https://...).

description.description: One line on what it tracks.

fields.description: The columns, 1 to 15. The first required one is usually a date.

choices.description: The allowed values, for type enum.

health.description: For source health: the phone health value that fills this column, read by the TrackerHacker iPhone or Android app from Apple Health or Health Connect over each row's time (see health_rows), combined as how says. Sleep's parts are asleep, rem, deep, light, awake or inBed (unit hours or minutes); blood pressure's are systolic or diastolic; workouts' are minutes or count, and on a sheet with a row per workout also id (a text column, the row's key), start (datetime), activity and source (text), distance, calories, heartRate and maxHeartRate. Numbers go in number columns.

how.description: How the readings in a row's time become one value, like the lowest glucose during a workout; each type has its own default.

meaning.description: What the value means: units, sign, what's included.

health.description: The Apple Health type, for source health, like "Sleep".

health_rows.description: For source health, how often a row comes: day (the default; needs a date column), hour (needs a datetime column), workout (needs a text column with the workout's id; any other health column is read over the workout, like average heart rate or lowest glucose during it), or reading (each reading of one kind, like every glucose or blood pressure reading; needs a datetime column). Workout rows are sent as soon as a workout ends; the others when the phone app opens.

mail.description: The person's mail app, for email sources.

notify.description: Whether to notify the person about new rows the sheet asks about.

when.description: For health: send yesterday's value in the morning, or today's in the evening.
